\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഓവർടൈം} (ōvarṭaiṁ)}{ഓവർടൈം (ōvarṭaiṁ)}]{\ml{ഓവർടൈം} (ōvarṭaiṁ) — overtime}

\label{lesson:ML-C544-ovartaim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to dismiss, then the Malayalam for an employer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഓവർടൈം}}
\textbf{\ml{ഓവർടൈം}} — \emph{ōvarṭaiṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}overtime\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പണി} \ml{തീർക്കാൻ} \ml{അവൻ} \ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{ഓവർടൈം} \ml{ചെയ്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paṇi tīrkkān avan innale ōvarṭaiṁ ceytu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He worked overtime yesterday to finish the job.
\end{quote}

\ml{ഓവർടൈം} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}, to work overtime.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഓവർടൈം}} (\emph{ōvarṭaiṁ}) was borrowed from English \emph{overtime}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōvarṭaiṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōvarṭaiṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṇi tīrkkān avan innale ōvarṭaiṁ ceytu.} — He worked overtime yesterday to finish the job.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to dismiss, then the Malayalam for an employer, then say \emph{ōvarṭaiṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഓവർടൈം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Overtime\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സംരംഭം} (saṁrambhaṁ)}{സംരംഭം (saṁrambhaṁ)}]{\ml{സംരംഭം} (saṁrambhaṁ) — a venture; an enterprise}

\label{lesson:ML-C544-samrambham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an employer, then the Malayalam for overtime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സംരംഭം}}
\textbf{\ml{സംരംഭം}} — \emph{saṁrambhaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a venture; an enterprise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൾ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{ചെറിയ} \ml{ബേക്കറി} \ml{സംരംഭം} \ml{തുടങ്ങി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ oru ceṟiya bēkkaṟi saṁrambhaṁ tuṭaṅṅi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She started a small bakery venture.
\end{quote}

A word of business news; \ml{സംരംഭം} \ml{തുടങ്ങുക}, to start a venture.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സംരംഭം}} (\emph{saṁrambhaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{saṁrambha}, which CDIAL glosses as vehemence (CDIAL 12993); Malayalam uses it for an undertaking pursued with zeal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrambhaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrambhaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷ oru ceṟiya bēkkaṟi saṁrambhaṁ tuṭaṅṅi.} — She started a small bakery venture.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an employer, then the Malayalam for overtime, then say \emph{saṁrambhaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സംരംഭം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A venture; an enterprise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സംരംഭകൻ} (saṁrambhakan)}{സംരംഭകൻ (saṁrambhakan)}]{\ml{സംരംഭകൻ} (saṁrambhakan) — an entrepreneur}

\label{lesson:ML-C544-samrambhakan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for overtime, then the Malayalam for a venture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സംരംഭകൻ}}
\textbf{\ml{സംരംഭകൻ}} — \emph{saṁrambhakan} — \textquotedblleft{}an entrepreneur\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{സംരംഭകൻ} \ml{ഗ്രാമത്തിലെ} \ml{പത്ത്} \ml{പേർക്ക്} \ml{ജോലി} \ml{കൊടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā saṁrambhakan grāmattile pattŭ pērkkŭ jōli koṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That entrepreneur gave jobs to ten people in the village.
\end{quote}

A woman is \ml{സംരംഭക}. -\ml{അകൻ} marks the one who does something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സംരംഭകൻ}} (\emph{saṁrambhakan}) is built on \ml{സംരംഭം}, from Sanskrit \emph{saṁrambha} (CDIAL 12993), with the agent ending -\ml{അകൻ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrambhakan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrambhakan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā saṁrambhakan grāmattile pattŭ pērkkŭ jōli koṭuttu.} — That entrepreneur gave jobs to ten people in the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for overtime, then the Malayalam for a venture, then say \emph{saṁrambhakan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്} (ṣiphṟṟŭ)}{ഷിഫ്റ്റ് (ṣiphṟṟŭ)}]{\ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്} (ṣiphṟṟŭ) — a work shift}

\label{lesson:ML-C544-siphrru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a venture, then the Malayalam for an entrepreneur.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്}} — \emph{ṣiphṟṟŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a work shift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ചേച്ചിക്ക്} \ml{അടുത്ത} \ml{ആഴ്ച} \ml{രാത്രി} \ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്} \ml{ആണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cēccikkŭ aṭutta āḻca rātri ṣiphṟṟŭ āṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My elder sister is on the night shift next week.
\end{quote}

Day and night shifts: \ml{പകൽ} \ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്}, \ml{രാത്രി} \ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഷിഫ്റ്റ്}} (\emph{ṣiphṟṟŭ}) was borrowed from English \emph{shift}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣiphṟṟŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cēccikkŭ aṭutta āḻca rātri ṣiphṟṟŭ āṇŭ.} — My elder sister is on the night shift next week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a venture, then the Malayalam for an entrepreneur, then say \emph{ṣiphṟṟŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മുടങ്ങുക} (muṭaṅṅuka)}{മുടങ്ങുക (muṭaṅṅuka)}]{\ml{മുടങ്ങുക} (muṭaṅṅuka) — to be interrupted; to stop midway}

\label{lesson:ML-C544-mutannuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an entrepreneur, then the Malayalam for a work shift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മുടങ്ങുക}}
\textbf{\ml{മുടങ്ങുക}} — \emph{muṭaṅṅuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to be interrupted; to stop midway\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മഴ} \ml{കാരണം} \ml{പണി} \ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{ദിവസം} \ml{മുടങ്ങി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻa kāraṇaṁ paṇi raṇṭŭ divasaṁ muṭaṅṅi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of the rain, work stopped for two days.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{മുടങ്ങി}, \emph{muṭaṅṅi}.

\ml{മുടക്കുക} is to stop something; \ml{മുടക്കം} is an interruption.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മുടങ്ങുക}} (\emph{muṭaṅṅuka}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 4933 gives it as to be hindered or obstructed (DEDR 4933).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṭaṅṅuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṭaṅṅuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻa kāraṇaṁ paṇi raṇṭŭ divasaṁ muṭaṅṅi.} — Because of the rain, work stopped for two days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an entrepreneur, then the Malayalam for a work shift, then say \emph{muṭaṅṅuka} again
\end{itemize}
